Quick technical notes from the bench:

- For TTFT accuracy, we'll pin sequence length to 256 and run 50 cold-start traces + 200 warm traces to capture KV cache behavior. p99 TTFT is sensitive to small scheduler queueing — we'll include 95th/99th tail graphs.
- Concurrency: to show sustainable QPS we recommend a mix of constant-rate windows (10m) and short bursts. Patchwork load (bursty traffic) will expose queueing latencies that matter for your UX.
- Model variants: we'll run both fp16 and a 4-bit quantized candidate. Expect ~15–25% CPU/GPU throughput improvement on quantized runs; we'll surface quality diffs in the appendix.
- Kernel selection & infra: we'll log GPU kernel timings + driver version. If you want NVLink or multi-instance configs, flag that now — it changes ramp characteristics.

I uploaded the first benchmark_plan_v1.csv with sample endpoints and the ramp profiles. I can run the baseline TTFT on Apr 15 and post raw CSV by EOD Apr 16.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
